title: Ladder Logic Advanced PID (Cascade)
description: Schema for a Ladder Logic cascaded PID controller. One PID (slave) receives its setpoint from another PID (master):contentReference[oaicite:52]{index=52}, enabling a cascade (master-slave) architecture.

SP.description: Local setpoint (used if master or if not in cascade mode). For a slave PID in cascade mode, this is superseded by the cascade setpoint from the master loop:contentReference[oaicite:53]{index=53}.

CL.description: Cascade enable. Set true to engage cascade mode for this PID:contentReference[oaicite:54]{index=54}. The CT field determines if this is a Master or Slave controller.

CT.description: Cascade Type (role of this controller):contentReference[oaicite:55]{index=55}. 'Master' = primary loop (sends its output as SP to a slave); 'Slave' = secondary loop (receives SP from a master).

MasterLoopTag.description: If this controller is a Slave, specify the tag name of the Master PID loop providing the cascade setpoint:contentReference[oaicite:56]{index=56}. If Master (or not used), this can be null or '0'.

MAXCV.description: CV EU max (engineering units of the output):contentReference[oaicite:57]{index=57}. **Important**: For a Master PID, scale this to match the Slave's PV range:contentReference[oaicite:58]{index=58}. This ensures the master's 0–100% output corresponds to meaningful SP for the slave.

MINCV.description: CV EU min (engineering units of output). Align with Slave's PV range minimum for Master loops:contentReference[oaicite:59]{index=59}.
